page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture under the AWS Nitro hypervisor system. It features 16 dedicated physical cores based on the AWS Graviton2 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 32.0 GB of system memory yielding 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. It does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence, but supplies a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In synthetic and real-world benchmark evaluations, the c6gn.4xlarge exhibits balanced multi-threaded performance alongside modest single-core execution speed. Multi-core compute tests such as stress-ng (24,284.25) and Geekbench multi-core (8,613.0) place the instance within the average tier, supported by solid results in software compilation with Clang (15,107.0) and ray tracing tasks. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (956.0) and gzip compression (20.34 GB/sec), place in the lower quartile, reflecting the architectural clock rate and IPC constraints of the Neoverse-N1 core. Memory read throughput reaches 169.51 GB/sec on large blocks, while memory write reaches 71.54 GB/sec.

High-throughput in-memory data structures perform reliably on this instance, demonstrated by Redis SET performance reaching 18.45 million operations per second and static web throughput measuring 19.19 GB/sec. However, machine learning inference displays notable limitations, with small-model token generation running at 37.38 tokens per second and medium 7B model prompt processing achieving 16.13 tokens per second. The 25 Gbps network interface pairs well with the 16 dedicated ARM cores for scale-out, network-heavy applications, offering balanced resource density without hyperthreading overhead.

The c6gn.4xlarge is suitable for distributed containerized microservices, high-bandwidth web serving, continuous integration build clusters, and networked Redis caching layers optimized for the ARM64 instruction set. Workloads dependent on x86 vector extensions, high single-thread clock speed, or massive GPU acceleration should utilize alternative instance classes.
description: The Amazon Web Services c6gn.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 16-core AWS Graviton2 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It provides 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or discrete GPU hardware, relying on networked storage volumes. In benchmark testing, the platform demonstrates consistent average multi-core compute capability, scoring 8,613.0 in Geekbench multi-core and processing 18.45 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core execution speed and AI prompt processing remain modest. The absence of simultaneous multithreading provides predictable CPU performance across all 16 cores. This profile makes c6gn.4xlarge well suited for ARM-native software compilation, high-throughput network proxying, distributed web serving, and memory-conscious container deployments.
